extracted.intended_audience: graduate students applying for NIH NRSA (F31) fellowships and their sponsors/mentors
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing an NRSA F31 Ph.D. fellowship application (Research Strategy, Sponsor/Co-sponsor statements, Training Plan, and Responsible Conduct of Research training) that documents project design, mentoring, institutional resources, and trainee qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of bone architecture changes (microCT metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative changes in bone architecture that occur during S. aureus osteomyelitis will be measured with the assistance of the Vanderbilt University Institute of Imaging Science (VUIIS). To quantify bone remodeling, microCT will be used to measure cortical bone changes around the inoculation site and trabecular bone architecture, including bone volume/trabecular volume (BV/TV), trabecular thickness, trabecular spacing, and trabecular number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent imaging core resources (e.g., VUIIS). Report standard microCT metrics (BV/TV, trabecular thickness/spacing/number) and quantify cortical changes around inoculation site. Use mock-infected bones from same strain as uninfected healing controls to avoid confounding by genotype differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and quantification of osteoclast changes by histology
rubrics_metrics.description: Osteoclast changes during S. aureus osteomyelitis will be defined using histologic analyses of infected bone. Following microCT scans, femurs will be decalcified and embedded for sectioning and staining with bone-specific hematoxylin and eosin and TRAP stains. OCs will be quantified from histological sections by counting TRAP-positive MNCs next to trabeculae in infected or mock-infected femurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify decalcification, embedding, H&E and TRAP staining protocols. Quantify osteoclasts by counting TRAP-positive multinucleated cells adjacent to trabeculae; include details on sectioning and core facility support (e.g., Bone Histology core).

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo bone resorption activity assessment (calvarial injection model & dynamic histomorphometry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bone resorption activity of OCs will be monitored in vivo using a calvarial injection model, where concentrated S. aureus supernatants or vehicle control will be injected over the calvaria for 5 consecutive days. Resorption pits on calvaria will be quantified after 9 days using microCT analysis, and the mineral apposition rate (MAR) and bone formation rate (BFR) will be quantified using histologic measurement of calcein fluorescent double labels incorporated into the bone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define injection schedule (5 consecutive days) and endpoint (day 9). Use microCT to quantify resorption pits and use calcein double-labels to calculate MAR and BFR; include imaging and histology methods and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate control selection (mock-infected bones from same strain)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mock-infected bones will be used as an uninfected healing control relative to infected femurs from the same mouse strain to avoid direct comparisons between different mouse genotypes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls should be matched by strain; avoid direct genotype-to-genotype comparisons that could confound infection-induced changes. Consider scaffold-delivered heat-killed bacteria or supernatants to isolate bacterial component effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated results with potential problems and alternative approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Results, Potential Problems, and Alternative Approaches: expect changes in OC number and bone resorption in vivo following stimulation with live S. aureus or concentrated supernatants. It is possible that defects in immunocompromised mice will lead to higher bacterial burdens at day 14 post-infection, which will complicate bone destruction data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State expected outcomes and explicitly identify potential complications (e.g., higher bacterial burdens). Provide concrete alternative approaches to mitigate problems (e.g., use scaffolds eluting heat-killed bacteria or concentrated supernatants as described in prior manuscript).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear statement of respective contributions and candidate role
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship Application: I designed the studies, optimized the experiments, and generated all of the preliminary data included in this application. I will design and perform all of the experiments proposed in the Research Strategy, with some contributions from others. The advanced surgical techniques for the in vivo osteomyelitis model require Dr. Cassat; however, I will follow up with animal care and monitoring, as well as end point harvest and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly delineate which tasks the candidate will perform (design, optimization, experiments, staining, data interpretation, statistics) versus mentor/core contributions (technical support, advanced surgical techniques, embedding/sectioning). This clarifies training and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentoring and committee oversight frequency and function
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee meetings will be held biannually, chaired by Dr. Eric Skaar, and attended by co-sponsor and other committee members. These meetings will provide the opportunity for committee members to give feedback on proposed experiments and data analysis, which will further enhance the quality of the proposed Research Strategy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify meeting cadence (biannual), chair, attendees, and purpose (feedback on experiments and data analysis). Document routine mentor-trainee interactions (e.g., weekly one-on-ones, weekly lab meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for selection of institution
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of Institution: chosen for history of exceptional graduate education and extramural funding, access to core facilities led by experts, a highly collaborative environment, comprehensive coursework across degree-granting departments, and career development resources provided by the BRET Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justify institutional choice with specific features: core facilities, collaborative environment, coursework, and institutional career development programs (e.g., BRET ASPIRE). Provide examples of relevant cores and support available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for selection of sponsor
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of Sponsor: sponsor's research convergence with applicant interests (microbial pathogenesis, immune responses, skeletal biology), mentoring style (personalized project, time investment), and clinical experience (physician-scientist) guided the decision to join the sponsor's laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the sponsor's expertise, mentoring approach, and resources align with the applicant's training goals. Document prior interactions (rotations, presentations) that motivated the choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for selection of co-sponsor and cross-disciplinary training
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of Co-sponsor: co-sponsor provides bone biology expertise, training opportunities (mini-sabbatical), experience in bone histology techniques, and serves on the thesis committee to bridge bone biology and infectious disease expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe co-sponsor's complementary expertise, specific training activities (e.g., periodic training visits), and role on the thesis committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR) training structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: BRET RCR Training: Vanderbilt provides introductory and ongoing RCR training through the BRET Office to satisfy NIH RCR requirements. The BRET Office offers an introduction to laboratory ethics (2 hour course) covering plagiarism, fabrication, falsification, record keeping, data management, and sharing. An annual full-day (9 hour) RCR symposium addresses RCR issues outlined by the Office of Research Integrity (ORI) through lectures, case studies, and small group discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document both introductory and ongoing RCR training: timing (intro at orientation, annual symposium), duration (2-hour intro; 9-hour symposium), instructional formats (lectures, case studies, small groups), and core topics aligned to ORI expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCR syllabus must cover ORI nine areas (examples listed)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual RCR Symposium covers the nine areas of focus for RCR with ORI subject matter noted beneath each topic, including: (1) Overview of Institutional & NIH Policies regarding grants, research, animal use, and human subjects; (2) What biomedical scientists need to know about the NIH funding system; (3) Data Management, Record Keeping and Conflict of Interest; (4) Authorship and Publication; (5) Reproducibility; (6) Mentorship; etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure RCR training explicitly lists and covers the ORI nine focus areas with faculty presenters, case studies, and applied discussion. Include subtopics such as conflict of interest, peer review, responsible authorship, and policies for handling misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ongoing lab-based RCR training and integration into normal lab activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Ongoing Training in RCR: weekly individual meetings with sponsor to discuss research progress and ORI issues; RCR discussions in weekly lab meetings; lab meeting presentations covering each of the 9 areas of RCR every 1-2 months; mentoring opportunities such as assisting in peer review of manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate RCR into weekly mentoring and lab meetings, schedule periodic focused presentations on RCR topics, and provide practical experiences (manuscript peer review) under mentor guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Plan, Environment, and Research Facilities description
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Plan/Environment/Research Facilities: describe lab size and space, BSL designation, capital equipment, adjacent facilities, computer resources and software, imaging cores (e.g., CSAI/VUIIS) with modalities listed (MRI, CT, PET, SPECT, ultrasound, BLI, fluorescence), animal facility details (ABSL-2 housing, surgical suites), and institutional support units (DAC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete details: lab square footage, equipment inventory, BSL level, computing resources including backup/server access, and access to imaging cores and animal facilities. Demonstrate that facilities support proposed methods and biosafety needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document number of fellows/trainees and lab management to ensure adequate supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of Fellows/Trainees to be Supervised During the Fellowship: describe current lab composition (e.g., 5 individuals) and roles (graduate students, MSTP students, lab manager), noting that lab manager handles administrative tasks so the fellow can focus on research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current personnel, supervisory capacity, and administrative support to show the fellow will receive adequate mentorship and not be overburdened by non-research duties. Explain how peer trainees provide intellectual community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor's track record and training outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor's Previous Fellows and Trainees: document the sponsor's prior trainees, their career outcomes (e.g., number trained, tenure-track positions), and how senior mentors will support the fellow if the sponsor has limited prior mentees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide trainee counts, notable outcomes, and plans for additional senior mentorship if sponsor is junior; name co-mentors who will contribute expertise and committee roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant qualifications and evidence of potential for a research career
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant's Qualifications and Potential for a Research Career: describe prior training (Master's thesis work), publications (first-author, middle-author; manuscripts in revision), successful completion of coursework, passing dissertation candidacy exam, inclusion in programs like VPMM, and records of training others (teaching/training rotation students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific prior outputs (number of publications, journals), completed milestones (coursework, candidacy), participation in relevant training programs, and examples of leadership/teaching to demonstrate readiness for the fellowship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed listing of critical equipment and imaging modalities available
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment: list of major equipment relevant to the proposal (e.g., centrifuges, biosafety cabinets, microscopes, incubators, microplate reader, gel documentation, -80°C freezer, electroporation apparatus) and imaging core instruments (4.7T, 9.4T, 15.2T MRI, Xenogen IVIS, Scanco μCT, Siemens MicroCAT/ MicroPET/ NanoSPECT, CRI Maestro, Visen FMT, VisualSonics ultrasound).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an inventory showing availability of all methods required by the project (molecular biology, advanced imaging, and animal surgery). Cite specific core instruments and access arrangements.
